items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: You know one of my influences was a guy named Tim Hagans who was on Stan Kenton’s band before me. I took his place.

ctx.x: I love sort of aggressive articulation even when playing a ballad. And I think I heard that, and with Clifford too. [scats] Like you don’t have to just mumble everything even if you’re playing a ballad.
Yeah. That’s interesting. I agree with you. You know one of my influences was a guy named Tim Hagans who was on Stan Kenton’s band before me. I took his place. Tim is a

beautiful player and we are good friends, even though I don’t get to see him very often. But Tim is very aggressive. And those are big shoes to fill when I got on Kenton’s band. He went on to other things. And I think I got some of that aggressive articulation from him a bit. In fact there was a time when I had to kind of say, “I’ve got to stop sounding so much like Tim Hagans.” I mean he had a record come out years later and a friend of mine came up and said, “I heard a guy play and he sounds just like you.” And…
